ruling.recommended_action: Route to RydeHELP human review as a rider-conduct safety report: attach the chat transcript (F3, F4) and the keyword flag (F5) to the driver's report (F6); do not issue any automated fare or account ruling; note for the reviewer that no physical contact, injury or repeat conduct appears in the file, and advise the driver of the RydeHELP reporting path (and 995 / commercial-insurance route if any medical or legal follow-up is needed).
ruling.escalation_reason: Safety-tagged docket with threat/intimidation language confirmed in the system record: rider's chat message at 18:22 "Say that again and I will punch you" [F4], flagged by the keyword table ("punch") [F5], one minute after the driver's request not to smoke [F3], and repeated in the driver's report [F6]. No automated ruling is issued under SAFE-1. Reviewer should check: the chat log timestamps (18:21 driver, 18:22 rider) [F3][F4]; the keyword-flag record [F5]; whether the driver reported via RydeHELP at the time; whether any physical contact or injury occurred (none appears in the file) [F4][F6]; and whether the rider offers a competing account. Trip data show no driver-side irregularity (8.8 km vs 8.9 km optimal, -0.1 km; 13.3 min vs 16 min, -3.0 min) so the metered fare of $21.26 stands [F1][F2].

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the rider's long account history and clean 90-day record mean 'no account-level flag is warranted' asks the Judge to weigh profile facts toward a merits outcome; profile facts never decide a case alone and SAFE-1 routes this docket to human review instead of any automated account finding [F7][SAFE-1].

The route/fare point (8.8 km actual vs 8.9 km optimal, -0.1 km) is correct on the trip data and is reflected in the summary, but it is not part of the operative disposition: the case is a safety escalation, so no fare ruling is issued and the metered fare is left untouched [F1][F2][SAFE-1].

The claim that the clean trip data 'confirm the driver took the direct route and the dispute concerns only the rider's conduct' overreaches: the trip data are consistent with no driver-side deviation, but they cannot establish the rider's conduct or the safety question, which is left to the human reviewer under SAFE-1 [F1][F2][SAFE-1].

The assertion that threats require 'immediate termination and possible legal action' states a punitive outcome the policy does not authorize the automated layer to impose; SAFE-1 requires only escalation with a factual summary, and the merits and any penalty are for human handling [F4][F6][SAFE-1].
